mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX 20-day returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 9.5% signals a weak labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE > 9.5 and SPX 5-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 215 and the federal funds rate remains below 0.5%, it indicates a policy response to inflation that is not yet tightening, leading to positive equity returns as the market anticipates gradual monetary policy adjustments.
failure_condition: The correlation between the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL>215 and FEDFUNDS<0.5) and SPX 60-day returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS above 0.5% and rising by at least 0.1% over the last 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.5 and FEDFUNDS change > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: The correlation between the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS>0.5 and FEDFUNDS change>0.1% in 3 months) and SPX 20-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and SPX 20-day returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When residential sales (RSAFS) fall below 300,000, it indicates a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS < 300000 and SPX 5-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 500 and industrial production (INDPRO) remains above 95, it indicates a balanced economic expansion with strong consumer demand and stable manufacturing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between the trigger condition (HOUST>500 and INDPRO>95) and SPX 60-day returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase (defined by UNRATE below 9.5% and PAYEMS above 130,000), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to improving consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The correlation between the trigger condition (UNRATE<9.5 and PAYEMS>130000) and SPX 20-day returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
